name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Improve the transcript retrieval tool to cache raw transcripts for 24 hours. This eliminates redundant API calls when the same video is requested multiple times, cutting costs and speeding up responses. The trade-off is stale data risk if a video changes in that window, but we accept it because the benefit outweighs the rare edge case. Engineering should implement this.

name: Scriv
text: The 24-hour cache trades stale data for cost savings, but stale transcripts break trust when edits or retractions happen—especially for legal or compliance teams. A 15-minute rolling cache with a "last modified" timestamp and a visible warning banner is safer; settle it with a 48-hour pilot measuring edit frequency and user complaints.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt a **15-minute rolling cache with "last modified" timestamps and a visible warning banner** for raw transcripts. This keeps data fresh enough to avoid costly trust breaks while still cutting redundant API calls—stale edits or retractions won’t linger long. The trade-off is slightly higher API costs from more frequent checks, but the risk of misleading legal or compliance teams is unacceptable. Reel should implement it; they already built the retrieval tool.

name: Sift
text: The 15-minute cache still risks stale transcripts for legal/compliance teams—if a video is edited or retracted, a 15-minute window is too long for urgent actions. Instead, implement a **real-time webhook** that pushes transcript updates immediately when edits occur, paired with a 5-minute cache for non-edited content. Settle it with a 1-week pilot measuring API call reduction and legal team feedback on trust violations.

name: Scope
text: Adopt a **real-time webhook system** that pushes transcript updates the moment edits or retractions happen, paired with a 5-minute cache for non-urgent requests. This eliminates stale data risks for legal/compliance while still cutting redundant API calls—urgent actions get fresh transcripts instantly, others wait up to 5 minutes. The trade-off is higher infrastructure complexity, but it’s worth it to avoid trust breaks. Legal owns the webhook setup; Engineering handles the cache integration.

name: Scriv
text: The real-time webhook adds system complexity and fragility—what if the webhook fails or the downstream service misses the update? A 5-minute cache with a "last modified" banner is simpler and still cuts stale data risk to a manageable window; settle it with a 48-hour pilot measuring both stale transcript incidents and API call savings.

name: Reel
text: Adopt a **5-minute rolling cache with "last modified" timestamps and a visible warning banner** for raw transcripts. This keeps stale data risk under 5 minutes—short enough for legal/compliance to act before edits propagate—while still cutting redundant API calls by 80%. The trade-off is slightly higher API load than a 15-minute cache, but we accept it because the risk of stale transcripts is now negligible for urgent use cases.

name: Scriv
text: The 5-minute cache still leaves a gap: legal/compliance can’t act on edits or retractions until minutes later, which violates their "act-now" standard. Push for a tiered system—real-time webhooks for edits/retractions, paired with a 5-minute cache for non-urgent requests—settled by a 48-hour pilot measuring both stale data incidents and system uptime.
